correction: Render the existing fundamental-domain diagram using supported fenced TikZ in Remarks, preserving all coordinates, labels, colors, and pairings.

diagram_math_checks.objects: The rectangle represents a fundamental domain for R^2/(2 pi Z)^2, as defined in Example line 31; it is explicitly a topology schematic, not a metric-scale square.
diagram_math_checks.relations: The two horizontal edges share y=0~2 pi and the two vertical edges share x=0~2 pi. These express (x,0)~(x,2 pi) and (0,y)~(2 pi,y), preserving the other coordinate point-for-point.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Example opposite-side identification and Given line 37. The diagram has no arrows; it makes no induced boundary-orientation assertion. In coordinate terms paired seams identify equal increasing coordinates, rather than following the opposite induced orientations of a positively oriented square boundary.

diagram_math_checks.objects: The displayed velocity u and pressure p are periodic functions on the identified domain.
diagram_math_checks.relations: Each velocity component is a product of sine/cosine factors with 2 pi period; pressure factors cos(2x),cos(2y) also have 2 pi period. Repeated derivatives exchange sine and cosine and preserve the periodic seams.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Read local thm-sine-cosine-zero-sets-and-fundamental-period Statement and thm-sine-and-cosine-derivatives Statement; item F2/F3 and Verification 1.1. No velocity vectors, flow circulation, or vorticity are drawn or inferred from the boundary labels.

diagram_math_checks.objects: The diagram contains one complete rectangular outline and four exterior seam labels.
diagram_math_checks.relations: Two equal-labeled pairs encode the two periodic identifications, with all corners belonging to the same quotient class. Unchanged unequal drawn side lengths merely reflect the explicitly schematic rectangle.
diagram_math_checks.justification: Original TikZ source and explanatory paragraph, retained exactly except relocation reference. The proof Verification 1.1 and 2.1 is analytic and unchanged.
